text:
maya: Alert from hosted-usw3 GPU pool — admission_rejections spike + queue depth rising, p95 queueing ~ 2.3s and p99 ~ 6.7s. Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/hosted-usw3
jon: copying the alert, looks like a waterfall: a handful of heavy customers hitting per-route rate caps -> retries -> admission -> queueing. admission_rejections metric jumped from ~120/min to 7.8k/min in ~10m
maya: exact alert rule: hosted.usw3.gpu.admission_rejections > 2000 for 5m
linh: I see correlate with route: customer:borealis-prod — their concurrent limit is 40. Their incoming RPS spiked. Lots of 429s in the proxy logs followed by client retries.
nate: is this the same pattern as last month where overflow routing didn't kick?
jon: probably. The fallback policy to dedicated overflow was suppressed because the candidate pool showed insufficient headroom due to a bogus reservation leak.
arian: tagging @sre-oncall-bot to page when admission_rejections > 2k for >5m — already fired though
sre-oncall-bot: @oncall triggered: hosted:usw3 admission_rejections high — run runbook 'usw3-admission-spike'
maya: quick triage steps I'm running: 1) check pool headroom + eviction logs 2) inspect per-route concurrency table 3) temporarily bump client route cap if safe
jon: can we bump the per-route concurrency for customer:borealis-prod from 40 -> 80 as a temporary mitigation? They'll have higher token spend but reduces retry loop. Any objections?
linh: we can, but need quick cost notification to customer-success. Also watch backlog — we must ensure we don't starve reserved customers.
nate: if we bump, we should also set a 30m auto-revert. I can prepare the change via orchestration API.
jon: please add an audit tag. Command I used previously:
```
# increase per-route concurrency for a route
curl -X POST \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"route":"customer:borealis-prod","concurrent_limit":80,"expiry":"30m","reason":"temporary mitigation for admission spike 1732500000"}' \ 
  https://admin-api.redwood.internal/v1/routes/update
```
linh: also looking at pool allocation — there's a recurring job that leaked reservations last night at 02:08 UTC, evicter logs show repeated failure to free slots. Opening a ticket for infra to investigate eviction loop.
maya: making the API call to bump now. posting logs in case it helps:
```
2026-02-18T15:14:12Z hosted-usw3 admission_rejections=7812 p95_queue_ms=2300 pool_headroom=3
2026-02-18T15:15:05Z route=customer:borealis-prod active_conns=71 route_limit=40 retries_5m=1200
```
jon: after bumping, watch admission_rejections and queue length. If admission_rejections falls but latency rises a lot we need to revert. Also enable overflow to dedicated for this route as a longer-term fix.
linh: overflow candidate pool currently at 12% headroom — we should also drain low-priority workloads to make room. Will open an ops play to move ephemeral eval jobs to other regions.
nate: I've queued a reversible change: request-id 0x9af3b updated route concurrency -> 80, expiry 30m. Pushing note to change log.
arian: customer-success notified via DM. cost impact estimate for bump: +$1.2k/day if sustained; CS to confirm if acceptable.
sre-oncall-bot: update: hosted.usw3.admission_rejections returned to 450/min after 8m. p95 queue down to 420ms.
maya: good, looks like the bump temporarily broke the retry waterfall. Keeping monitoring for 30m then auto-revert. Follow-ups: 1) fix eviction leak 2) make overflow policies more permissive when pool headroom < 20% 3) add trend alert for per-route retries -> admission spikes
jon: also propose a throttling backoff change: signal clients with Retry-After and jitter to reduce synchronized retries. Could add to orchestration proxy as a short-term policy.
linh: filing infra ticket: INFRA-4822 "eviction-loop prevents overflow candidate selection" and linking logs.
maya: thanks all. leaving this thread open until auto-revert completes at 1732501800. If anything new pops up please call out with timestamp and request-id. :thumbsup:
